query: Which material can be used for enhance glass-forming ability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding a specific concentration of titanium dioxide (TiO2) to silica (SiO2) will enhance the glass-forming ability of the silica.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of titanium dioxide (TiO2) at varying concentrations into the silica matrix.
generation.conditions: Controlled atmosphere during melting and cooling processes to prevent contamination and ensure accurate measurements.
generation.structural_mediator: The presence of TiO2 modifies the network structure of SiO2, potentially increasing the connectivity and reducing the tendency to crystallize.
generation.mechanism: TiO2 acts as a network former, disrupting the crystalline order of SiO2 and promoting a more favorable glassy state during cooling.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in the glass-forming ability of the silica, indicated by a lower melting temperature and improved glass stability.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to the specific concentration range of TiO2 that is known to enhance glass-forming ability without causing adverse effects.
generation.uncertainty: The exact concentration of TiO2 that maximizes the glass-forming ability is uncertain and may vary based on other compositional factors.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a series of melting experiments with varying concentrations of TiO2 added to SiO2, followed by controlled cooling to form glass.
measurements: X-ray diffraction patterns to assess crystallinity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of TiO2 does not lower the melting temperature or improve the glass stability compared to pure SiO2, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
